ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (notably by the Law of 17 July 2020 and the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing EU Directive 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 January 2019 implementing it; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (governing the SARL); Legislation of 25 April 2018 on medicinal products (GDP storage authorization).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_public_access_note: The Luxembourg RBE is accessible to the CSSF, the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), duty-holders and obliged entities, tax authorities, and, under the framework of the European Court of Justice Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20, public access is restricted to holders of a legitimate interest; the register is not fully public.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_methodology: Mandatory identification of every individual ultimately owning or controlling, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of shares, voting rights, or an equivalent economic interest; for layered structures, each intermediate legal entity is pierced to its underlying natural persons; if no natural person is identified, senior managing officials are declared as pseudo-UBOs.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, managers, authorized signatories, and UBOs against (a) the Luxembourg consolidated financial sanctions list (Ministère des Finances), (b) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (c) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (d) OFAC SDN list as best practice for US nexus screening, and (e) FATF high-risk jurisdiction notifications. PEP status (office held within last 12 months) triggers enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and escalation to the CSSF reporting channel where necessary. Screening is refreshed at account opening, upon concentration threshold changes, and on an event-driven basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) portal at www.lbr.lu — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name may be drafted in French, German, Luxembourgish, or English, or any combination using the Latin script. Non-Latin scripts require a mandatory transliteration in Latin characters. The name must not be misleading, must not create a likelihood of confusion with existing reservations, and must respect public order and morality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (where official state authorization is falsely implied)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation can be extended once by 30 days upon payment of the additional official fee; if the RCS rejects the name, counsel shall first submit a reasoned re-submission with amended corporate name. If the rejection is definitively maintained, an administrative appeal is addressed to the President of the Tribunal de l'Arrondissement of Luxembourg in commercial matters within 3 months of notification of refusal. In exigent circumstances, an urgent interim order (procédure en référé) can be sought. Any name actually registered is subject to cancellation by the president of the district court on the grounds of prior third-party rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. The SARL must have a registered office in Luxembourg (Articles 98-101 of the Law of 10 August 1915). A purely virtual administrative address is not accepted for a concession/licensed refrigerated pharmaceutical warehouse; the operating site must be a physically accessible cold storage facility in Luxembourg. A managed/domiciliation office may serve as the statutory seat, provided the operational warehouse separately complies with Ministry of Health GDP inspection requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (approximately 15–20% per annum) for temperature-controlled pharmaceutical cold storage, driven primarily by unannounced Good Distribution Practice (GDP) inspections by the Direction de la Santé (Ministry of Health) and, where banking/AML obligations arise, targeted checks by the CSSF. Unannounced physical visits of the purely administrative statutory office are rare but legally permissible.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority (https://impotsdirects.public.lu) for corporate income tax and withholding tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) (https://aed.public.lu) for VAT, registration duties and excise; Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (ADA) for export clearance; unified e-administration and tax portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and PFI e-filing (https://pfiweb.etat.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SARL by deed before a Luxembourg notary and file the constitutive documents with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) (https://www.lbr.lu); the RCS issues the national business registration number (matricule), which is the master identifier for all subsequent tax files. Step 2 — Upon publication of the incorporation in the RCS, the company is automatically registered with the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; the ACD allocates the corporate tax file number; no separate application is required for a Luxembourg-resident SARL. Step 3 — Apply for Luxembourg VAT identification with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu using the form 'Demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA'; the AEDT issues a 7- or 8-digit Luxembourg VAT number prefixed 'LU' (format LU00000000). The application must be submitted before the first taxable supply. Step 4 — A non-resident foreign entity without a Luxembourg fixed establishment that carries out Luxembourg-taxable transactions must apply for direct VAT registration through the AEDT electronic portal before commencing activity; no de minimis turnover relief is available to non-established suppliers. Step 5 — Register as employer with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) where the SARL hires staff, and obtain the employer matricule for wage withholding and social security filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Luxembourg SARL is a fully taxable corporate entity (personne collective) resident in Luxembourg, subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune); no domestic pass-through election exists for a SARL (unlike SCS/SCSp partnerships, which may elect fiscal transparency). Available statutory mechanisms: (i) Fiscal Unity ('intégration fiscale') under Article 164bis LIR, permitting a Luxembourg-resident parent and Luxembourg-resident subsidiaries held directly or indirectly at a minimum 95% interest to elect aggregation of taxable results and intra-group loss offset; (ii) ATAD-compliant hybrid and imported hybrid mismatch counter-measures under Articles 168quater and 168quinquies LIR, which deny deductions where payments are tax-deductible in Luxembourg and non-includible, or doubly deductible, abroad; (iii) Participation Exemption under Article 166 LIR — 100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's capital or an acquisition price of at least EUR 1.2 million and the subsidiary is subject to a tax equivalent to Luxembourg corporate income tax; (iv) VAT grouping election ('assujetti unique') for consolidation of intra-group VAT positions. No US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification_notes: The SARL is a resident corporation fully liable to Luxembourg corporate income tax on worldwide income, subject to tax treaty relief and the domestic participation exemption; it is not a flow-through vehicle for Luxembourg domestic tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), implemented by the Law of 12 February 1979 (Loi TVA) in alignment with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established small enterprises (Article 55 Loi TVA); a Luxembourg SARL engaged in cold-storage warehousing will almost always exceed this threshold and must register from the first euro of taxable turnover once exceeded. Non-established foreign suppliers enjoy no de minimis threshold and must register for VAT from their first taxable transaction in Luxembourg. Intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers are subject to the EUR 10,000 annual cross-border threshold (Article 58 Loi TVA), after which VAT applies in the customer's Member State via the OSS regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority pre-clearance (SDI-style), or digital stamping mandate applies to B2B VAT invoices in Luxembourg. Mandatory electronic invoicing exists exclusively in the B2G segment: under the Law of 6 October 2021, suppliers invoicing Luxembourg central government entities must issue e-invoices through the PEPPOL network using Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 via a certified access point, with phased mandatory compliance completed for central contracting authorities from 1 January 2025. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and may be implemented by bilateral EDI or PEPPOL XML agreement. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (VIDA) proposals, which would introduce mandatory e-invoicing and digital reporting for intra-EU B2B transactions, are expected to apply from 1 July 2030 but are not yet in force. The SARL must submit periodic VAT returns (monthly/quarterly) electronically via the PFI portal and file the Intrastat and recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) where intra-EU supplies occur.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported goods under Article 41(3) Loi TVA applies where: (i) the SARL is a taxable person identified for VAT in Luxembourg; (ii) the goods are physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union; (iii) the goods leave the EU within 90 days of the supply or within the normal contractual dispatch timeline; and (iv) the export declaration (SAD/DAU) is lodged electronically with the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (ADA) and the corresponding Movement Reference Number (MRN) and transport documents are retained. Where the SARL supplies cold-chain storage, handling and ancillary logistics services to a taxable recipient established outside the EU, the supply falls outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule (Articles 14 and 41 Loi TVA), or is zero-rated where directly connected to exported goods; the SARL must obtain the customer's foreign VAT identification number and retain contractual and delivery evidence. Intra-EU cold-storage services supplied to EU taxable persons are taxable in the customer's Member State under the reverse-charge mechanism, with the SARL required to file recapitulative statements and monitor the EUR 10,000 OSS threshold for any B2C supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / DAU) endorsed by the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (ADA), including the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and entry of the transport and destination details
Transport document proving physical departure from the EU: Bill of Lading (maritime), CMR waybill (road), Air Waybill (air), or multimodal transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/bank transfer evidence demonstrating settlement of the export proceeds by the foreign customer
Commercial invoice and packing list referencing the exported goods and the VAT zero-rating or outside-scope basis
Cold-chain custody and temperature-monitoring records (time-stamped logger data) evidencing continuous temperature-controlled storage from intake through dispatch
Warehouse stock ledgers, inventory movement registers, and customs warehouse or authorised storage authorisation documents applicable to the refrigerated logistics facility
Purchase invoices and import documentation substantiating input VAT allocation to the exported goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export VAT zero-rating claims are subject to ex-post documentary audits by the AEDT (VAT) and customs post-clearance verification by the ADA; the taxpayer must produce the complete documentary bundle within the statutory response period (generally 30 days). Deficiencies or inconsistencies in documentation lead to retrospective clawback of the zero-rated VAT, plus statutory late-payment interest. Fraudulent or recklessly unsupported claims trigger: (i) administrative penalties under Article 81 Loi TVA and the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung — AO LUX) of up to 100% of the evaded differential tax; (ii) criminal sanctions for tax fraud and customs fraud under Articles 395-396 AO LUX and Article 82 Loi TVA, with fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of the responsible directors and managers; (iii) joint and several civil liability of the SARL's directors and liquidators under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies for tax deficiencies arising from non-compliance; (iv) withdrawal of the customs warehouse or AEO status, cancellation of export licences, exclusion from the OSS and IOSS schemes, and publication on the AEDT list of delinquent taxable persons; (v) a five-year retroactive assessment window under Article 225 AO LUX, extended where fraud or concealment is established. The SARL should therefore maintain a formal export compliance file ('preuve d'exportation') assembled at the time of each zero-rated supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank; banking prudential and AML/CFT supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully liberalized regime: the euro is fully convertible, and Luxembourg applies no exchange-control approvals, no capital-export restrictions, and no prior authorization for profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayment, or liquidation proceeds. Both current-account and capital-account transactions benefit from the free movement of capital under TFEU Articles 63-65, subject only to EU-wide prudential safeguards, national security screening, and statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations to the BCL. For a Luxembourg SARL invoicing in EUR within the eurozone, no convertibility exposure exists; cross-currency USD/CHF/GBP receipts are convertible at market rates without reference to the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg does not impose any statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation-surrender requirement for export proceeds, including warehouse logistics service receipts from third countries. The SARL may freely retain, convert, hedge, or reinvest export earnings in EUR or any other convertible currency.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility as a supplemental payment-collection channel, but not viable as the primary treasury and clearing bank. Luxembourg-licensed E-Money Institutions under the CSSF E-Money Law 2010 and PSD2 can conduct SEPA credit transfers, FX conversion, and virtual multi-currency accounts, but they cannot issue or confirm Commercial Letters of Credit, provide UCP600 documentary trade services, hold BCL settlement reserves, or grant overdraft/working-capital facilities. For a cold-storage logistics SARL servicing pharma clients, the recommended architecture is a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution for all account-balance, escrow, trade, and liquidity functions, with a supervised EMI (e.g., licensed Luxembourg branch of Airwallex, Currencies Direct, or similar) restricted to cross-border receivable acceleration and automated reconciliation, subject to daily sweeping of balances into the Tier-1 bank and contractual client-fund safeguarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for at least one authorized signatory and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), or for a notarized attorney holding a specific power of attorney: Luxembourg banks apply CSSF Regulation 12-02 and frequently require an in-branch identity and source-of-funds interview. Fully remote onboarding is available only for low-risk EU-domiciled UBOs through video-identification at banks such as BIL and BGL BNP Paribas, but in practice a SARL with non-resident shareholders and a regulated logistics license will face face-to-face compliance due diligence at the bank's Luxembourg office. A Luxembourg notary can authenticate a written proxy for the gérant and attest passport copies; the bank may also accept verification certificates issued by a senior foreign correspondent bank for non-EU shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO not registered in the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) before account opening; banks are legally required to consult the RBE and cannot open an account for an unregistered entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Confirmed RBE filing receipt, notarized articles of association, current share register extract, a signed beneficial-ownership declaration by the gérant, and passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; register the UBO with the Luxembourg Business Registers prior to signing any bank mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU shareholders with an opaque ownership chain or complex intermediate holding vehicles, triggering enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, clean sanctions/PEP screening consent, bank reference letter from each shareholder's Tier-1 institution, audited financial statements or notarized capital-origin statement, full organizational chart with LEI numbers, and notarized confirmation of economic justification for the Luxembourg SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cold-chain warehousing for pharmaceuticals flagged for potential controlled-substance, dual-use, or counterfeit-goods exposure under the bank's sectoral risk policy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Luxembourg warehouse license, Good Distribution Practice (GDP) certificate, temperature-mapping validation reports, procedure manuals for quarantine and destruction, customer list limited to licensed pharma manufacturers and wholesalers, and contractual prohibition of controlled-substance or investigational-drug handling without prior bank notification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance or tax residency proof, leading the bank to treat the SARL as a domiciliation-vehicle red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificat de résidence fiscale (form 100) issued by the Luxembourg tax office, lease agreement for physical warehouse/premises, CCSS social-security registration for employees, local insurance policies, utility bills, and a board-approved business plan evidencing local management and operational independence from the foreign parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border USD/CHF flows from non-EU pharma counterparties triggering sanctions, embargo, or trade-interdiction filter hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-signed trade contracts listing each counterparty, final consignee and Incoterms, dedicated OFAC/EU consolidated-list screening reports, customs and export declarations, and a written undertaking that the SARL will not route goods, funds, or services through sanctioned jurisdictions including Russia, Belarus, Iran, Crimea, North Korea, and Syria.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital formation and subsequent capital increases must be routed through a Luxembourg credit institution holding a capital-blocking certificate (attestation bancaire de blocage) for notarization; for a SARL the statutory minimum capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash. The compliant routing is: shareholder instructs its foreign bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-resident shareholders) to the SARL's account at BIL/BGL/BCEE using the SARL's IBAN LUxx, with field 70 remittance information: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION LU_SARL — FORMATION/INCREASE, NOTARY DEED [date], RCS LUXEMBOURG [number]'; the bank will freeze the funds until the notary confirms completion of incorporation and issuance of court-approved RCS extract. For balance-of-payments statistics, classify the flow as direct-investment equity capital under BCL/Eurosystem reporting; the bank includes the capital-blocking certificate in the notarial file. No prior BCL approval is required for inbound euro transfers, but the source of funds must be documented for AML purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Eurozone suppliers are paid by SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant using ISO 20022 pain.001 messages; cross-border non-EU trade disbursements use SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers with full beneficiary identifiers and reference to the underlying warehouse-services or logistics invoice. For larger multi-country equipment purchases, the SARL may instruct Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) or standby letters of credit (ISP98) through BGL BNP Paribas or BIL, but standby/LC usage is expected to be rare for a low-risk storage business; open-account MT103 rails are preferred. Outbound dividends and shareholder-loan repayments require a separate MT103 with reference to the general meeting decision, the audited financial statements, and the applicable double-tax-treaty article; Luxembourg domestic dividend withholding of 15% applies unless reduced under treaty, and the paying bank may ask for a tax-residence certificate of the shareholder. All outbound transfers are subject only to transaction-based BCL statistical reporting thresholds and CSSF/EU funds-tracing rules; there is no exchange-control approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright deliverable FX forwards with maturity up to 12 months under an ISDA 2002 or bank standard master agreement; permitted only against documented underlying USD-denominated warehousing receivables or payables.
EUR/CHF and EUR/GBP deliverable FX forwards for Swiss-pound and sterling-invoiced pharma clients; tenor matched to the commercial invoice cycle and limited to 100% of notional exposure.

EUR/USD and EUR/CHF cross-currency swaps for capital-expenditure or shareholder-loan liabilities exceeding EUR 5 million notional; subject to EMIR margining, clearing, and trade-reporting obligations applicable to non-financial counterparties above the clearing threshold.

FX options and zero-cost collar structures (EUR call / USD put) on forecast USD receipts, with an internal policy capping delta exposure at 25% of the next 12-month forecast and requiring senior-management approval.
FX spot outright transactions (T+2) for routine treasury conversion via the bank's electronic dealing desk.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for a Luxembourg-resident SARL as a primary hedge because the euro is fully convertible; NDFs are limited to hedges of subsidiary-entity cash flows located in currencies with capital controls, and even then only through a licensed Luxembourg credit institution with IFRS 9 fair-value accounting and full EMIR documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, P&L, notes) filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filed with the RCS by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal notice, administrative fines up to €2,000, court-ordered filing at the company's expense, and possible striking-off from the RCS upon persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the anniversary date of the initial UBO registration; any change in shareholding must be declared within 1 month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or update is punishable by an administrative fine up to €5,000 per entity; repeated non-compliance may lead to daily fines and criminal prosecution of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the tax year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, the return is due by 30 June of the following year, unless a justified extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 0.75% of the tax due per month, capped at 10%; ex officio assessment and interest on late payment at 0.6% per month in case of unpaid taxes

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises is required if the SARL exceeds at least two of these three criteria for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total above €4.4 million; net turnover above €8.8 million; average staff above 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for public-interest entities, parent companies preparing consolidated accounts, and certain regulated sectors (e.g., credit institutions, insurance, IFM).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Comptes annuels simplified under the Law of 19 December 2002) for unlisted SARL; IFRS as adopted by the EU for consolidated financial statements and optionally for statutory accounts of listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain a current UBO file with the RBE and complete an annual confirmation before the anniversary of the initial filing. Any share transfer, change of control, or other change in beneficial ownership must be declared within one month. The board of managers must certify the accuracy of the UBO data and evidence compliance at the AGM.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders (share ledger with share transfers)
Minute book of shareholders' meetings and management resolutions
Register of financial movements/inventory if required by law

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate standard rate for Luxembourg City (CIT 17% + unemployment surcharge 7% of CIT + municipal business tax 6.75%); municipal business tax varies by commune of the exploitation centre.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income (effective rate ~5.17%); participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (0% effective); R&D super deduction: 6% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenditures; investment tax credit: 4% credit on qualifying cold-chain capex.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carrying forward under Luxembourg law; no statutory expiry; no carryback).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 700 (Modèle 700) - combined corporate income tax (IRAPC), municipal business tax (ISC) and net wealth tax (IFI) return; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / eTax (Fiscussinternet) portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (form 700); advance payment instalments are set by the AED and are not filed quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end for e-filings; paper filings have earlier administrative deadlines; extensions are granted by the AED on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Luxembourg RCS registration number, tax ID (matricule), registered office, legal form (SARL), director names.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for resident SARL; non-resident shareholders are identified in the shareholder annex for withholding tax purposes only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit/loss before tax under Lux GAAP, with attached balance sheet and profit-and-loss account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign passive income must be included; non-resident partners without a Luxembourg PE have no entry here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses: corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, fines, non-arm's-length management fees and excessive interest on shareholder loans.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-back of Luxembourg PE branch remittances not deductible; intercompany royalty payments must be substantiated by an underlying cost analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions applied: 80% IP-box exemption on qualifying IP income, participation exempt dividends, investment allowances, tax-exempt government subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are claimed only under an applicable DTA; otherwise a deduction for foreign taxes under ordinary law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result: accounting profit/loss plus réintégrations minus déductions; this is the base for CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a Luxembourg PE must attach the PE annex and compute Luxembourg-source taxable result separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses carried forward; unlimited carryforward period; requires supporting prior assessments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE losses are ring-fenced to the Luxembourg PE and cannot offset foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of exempt dividends and capital gains from qualifying EU and non-EU participations (>=10% or cost >= EUR 1.2 million, held >=12 months).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable to a Luxembourg-resident shareholder; a foreign parent cannot claim the exemption on dividends received from the Luxembourg SARL in this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax (ISC) base after applying the standard profit deduction and loss carryforward rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attributable Luxembourg PE capital and profits are included in the ISC base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing schedule: controlled transactions (storage fees, rents, royalties, interest) with counterparty jurisdiction, amount and method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose intercompany contracts with the foreign parent/affiliates; attach Local File and Master File where documentation thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: progressive fine up to EUR 2,500; failure to file triggers summary assessment (taxation d'office) with a 10% surcharge; late tax payment attracts 0.6% monthly default interest; intentional fraud carries criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax on distributions by a Luxembourg SARL; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying corporate shareholders (>=10% interest or >= EUR 1.2 million participation held >=12 months); DTA reductions typically 5% for direct holdings >=10% and 15% for portfolio holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief at source: the Luxembourg payer submits the shareholder's tax-residence certificate (TRC), proof of beneficial ownership, and holding-period evidence (12-month commitment) to the AED registration office; a reduced/zero withholding certificate is then issued. Refund route: if 15% was withheld, the non-resident shareholder files a Luxembourg tax refund request with TRC annexed no later than 31 December of the third year following the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties to non-residents (no domestic levy; no treaty reduction needed). Interest: 0% statutory withholding tax for arm's-length interest (exception: interest on profit-participating and convertible loans is recharacterised as a dividend and taxed at 15% WHT).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: annual related-party controlled transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 trigger mandatory contemporaneous local documentation. Master File: required where the group's consolidated annual net turnover reaches EUR 750 million. Thresholds are in EUR.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No freestanding Economic Substance Regulations (UAE-style) exist in Luxembourg; substance is enforced through (i) place of effective management/central administration for tax residence, (ii) beneficial ownership requirements for DTA and EU Directive relief, (iii) the Luxembourg GAAR / abuse-of-law doctrine, (iv) ATAD interest limitation (30% EBITDA) and anti-hybrid rules, and (v) the anticipated EU Unshell Directive tests. A cold-storage SARL must maintain physical premises, employees, board meetings and logistics decision-making in Luxembourg; an offshored management fee or booking-shell structure will be recharacterised and denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly under-reporting refrigerated warehousing and storage revenues; issuing fictitious invoices for intercompany cold-storage services; shifting profits to zero-tax affiliates without legitimate substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud: fine of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment of 2 to 10 years (aggravated); administrative reassessment at 100% of evaded CIT/WHT; default interest at 0.6% per month; possible publication of sanction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing directors (gérants) face criminal liability, personal fines, imprisonment, travel bans and asset freezes; civil courts may order restitution of evaded taxes and disqualification from board positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit the annual Luxembourg corporate tax return by the statutory deadline or refusal to e-file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing fine of EUR 250 to EUR 2,500; summary assessment (taxation d'office) with 10% surcharge; 0.6% monthly default interest on sums due; recovery costs charged to the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives remain personally exposed to fines; the tax authority can seize the director's personal estate where corporate assets are insufficient; flagrant recidivism leads to criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SARL operating as a letterbox with no cold-storage facilities, staff or management in Luxembourg; artificial routing of warehousing profits to foreign shareholders; sham storage service arrangements with related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the entity as fiscally transparent; denial of Luxembourg tax residence; refusal of participation exemption; re-allocation of profits to the foreign beneficial owner; 15% deemed-dividend WHT assessments; denial of DTA benefits under beneficial-ownership/GAAR analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and resident directors may be held personally liable for complicity in abuse of law; civil restitution orders for unpaid WHT/CIT; travel bans or entry restrictions during tax-criminal investigations; disqualification as Luxembourg statutory directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not preparing a Local File where intercompany storage rent, logistics fees or royalty charges exceed EUR 100,000 per year; submitting documentation later than 45 days of an AED request; pricing outside arm's length without a benchmarking study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EUR 2,500 for missing documentation; re-assessment of taxable income to the arm's-length profit; 0.6% monthly default interest; burden of proof shifts to taxpayer; risk of double taxation and additional penalties for gross negligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's-length intercompany fees without a transfer-pricing study can be sued for corporate loss; the tax authority may pierce the veil to enforce the TP adjustment against directors' personal assets in cases of gross negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the SARL's ultimate beneficial owner declaration in the Luxembourg RBE register within 30 days of incorporation; failure to conduct CDD/KYC for warehouse clients or foreign shareholders; concealment of UBO identity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover for serious AML breaches (Law of 22 January 2023); imprisonment up to 3 years for individuals; RBE register fines between EUR 500 and EUR 25,000 per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for AML fines; personal criminal conviction; travel bans and seizure of personal assets; civil liability to third parties for damages caused by missing UBO filings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or deemed distributions (surplus shareholder current account, excessive interest, shareholder loan waivers) without retaining 15% Luxembourg WHT; fraudulent reliance on a treaty-residence certificate of the parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of 15% WHT on the gross distribution plus 0.6% monthly default interest; penalty of up to 100% of evaded WHT in bad-faith cases; criminal fine of EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for fraudulent schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant acts as state collection agent; personal joint and several liability for the unwithheld WHT; seizure of director assets; travel bans pending recovery; disqualification from management of Luxembourg companies.
